description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a world-renowned Indian dish featuring tender chicken pieces bathed in a rich, creamy tomato-based gravy. This classic recipe balances smoky marinated chicken with sweet, tangy tomatoes and a luxurious finish of butter and cream, creating an unforgettable culinary experience. It is the epitome of comfort food, perfect for family dinners or entertaining guests.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: pureed (about 2 cups) or 1 (14.5 oz) can crushed tomatoes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter or oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through. Remove chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add finely chopped onion and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree, Kashmiri red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, until the tomato mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate from the sides.

instructions.title: Finish the Gravy
instructions.text: Add garam masala, crushed kasoori methi, sugar, and salt to the tomato mixture. Pour in 1/2 cup of water and bring to a gentle simmer. For a smoother texture, you can blend the gravy with an immersion blender or pass it through a fine-mesh sieve at this stage.

instructions.title: Combine and Serve
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken pieces back into the gravy. Stir well to coat the chicken. Pour in the heavy cream and simmer for another 5-7 minutes over low heat, allowing the flavors to meld and the gravy to thicken slightly. Adjust seasoning as needed. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot.

tips: For the best flavor, marinate the chicken overnight in the refrigerator. This allows the spices to deeply penetrate the meat, making it more tender and flavorful.
To achieve a silky-smooth gravy, pass the cooked tomato-onion mixture through a fine-mesh sieve or blend it thoroughly with an immersion blender before adding the chicken and cream.
Always add heavy cream at the very end and simmer gently to prevent it from curdling. A splash of milk can be substituted for cream, but cream provides the authentic richness.
article:
Unraveling the Richness of Butter Chicken: A Culinary Journey into Classic Murgh Makhani

Few dishes evoke the warmth and comfort of Indian cuisine quite like Butter Chicken. Known globally as Murgh Makhani, this iconic dish is a symphony of flavors, a delicate balance of tangy tomatoes, rich cream, fragrant spices, and succulent chicken. It’s a staple on restaurant menus worldwide and a cherished recipe in countless homes, embodying the essence of Indian culinary heritage. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality Butter Chicken in your own kitchen, this comprehensive guide will walk you through every step, ensuring a truly unforgettable experience. Get ready to master the art of Classic Murgh Makhani.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani as it's traditionally known, is a beloved Indian curry that originated in Delhi, India, in the 1950s. Its creation is often attributed to Kundan Lal Gujral, one of the founders of the Moti Mahal restaurant, who reputedly combined leftover tandoori chicken with a rich, tomato-based gravy. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," perfectly describing its key components. At its heart, it's a mild, creamy, and subtly spiced curry characterized by its vibrant orange-red hue and incredibly tender chicken pieces, often marinated and cooked separately before being submerged in the luscious sauce. The sauce itself is a masterpiece of slow-cooked tomatoes, aromatic ginger and garlic, a blend of traditional Indian spices, and a generous finish of butter and cream, which impart its signature velvety texture and luxurious taste. It’s a dish that appeals to all palates, from spice enthusiasts to those who prefer a milder flavor profile, making it a universal favorite.

## Ingredients for Classic Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a careful selection of fresh ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken (thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces)
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon cumin powder
*   Salt to taste

For the Makhani (Butter Chicken) Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (700g) can crushed tomatoes or 4-5 large ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, then drained)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon cumin powder
*   1/2 teaspoon coriander powder
*   1/2 teaspoon fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
*   1/2-1 teaspoon sugar or honey (to balance acidity)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or light cream for a lighter version)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## How to Make Butter Chicken: Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps meticulously for an authentic and delicious Butter Chicken:

Step 1: Marinate the Chicken
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally, for 4-6 hours (or even overnight) for maximum flavor and tenderness.

Step 2: Cook the Marinated Chicken
Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, making sure not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

Step 3: Prepare the Sauce Base
In the same pan (add a little more oil if needed), melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

Step 4: Build the Flavor and Simmer
Add the crushed tomatoes (or tomato puree) to the pan, along with the soaked and drained cashews, water/broth, and all the dry spices for the sauce (red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, cumin, coriander). Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the sauce has thickened slightly. The oil should begin to separate from the mixture.

Step 5: Blend and Strain for Smoothness
Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until perfectly smooth. For an extra velvety texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing down to extract all the liquid and leaving behind any fibrous bits. This step is crucial for that classic restaurant-style creamy finish.

Step 6: Finish the Butter Chicken
Return the smooth sauce to the pan over low heat. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces. Add the sugar or honey, the crushed kasoori methi, and season with salt to taste. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and a knob of butter. Heat through gently, but do not boil after adding the cream, as it can curdle. Garnish with fresh cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani

Achieving restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few expert tips:
*   **Chicken Thighs are King:** While chicken breast can be used, boneless, skinless chicken thighs are far superior for Murgh Makhani. They remain incredibly tender and juicy even after cooking, absorbing the rich flavors beautifully.
*   **Marination Time:** Don't skimp on the marination. The longer the chicken marinates, the more flavorful and tender it will become. Overnight marination is ideal.
*   **Quality Tomatoes:** Use good quality canned crushed tomatoes (like San Marzano) for consistent flavor and color. If using fresh, ensure they are very ripe and sweet.
*   **Cashews for Richness:** The cashews are not just for thickening; they add a subtle sweetness and a luxurious richness to the sauce that is characteristic of authentic Butter Chicken. Don't skip them!
*   **The Sieve is Your Friend:** Blending the sauce until smooth is important, but straining it afterward is what truly gives it that silky, restaurant-like texture. It removes any remaining onion or tomato skins and fibers.
*   **Kasoori Methi (Fenugreek Leaves):** This spice is non-negotiable for authentic Murgh Makhani flavor. Lightly toast the dried leaves in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing them between your palms and adding them to the sauce for maximum aroma.
*   **Balance is Key:** The sugar or honey is vital to balance the acidity of the tomatoes. Adjust to your taste, adding a little more if your tomatoes are particularly tart.
*   **Gentle Heat for Cream:** Once the cream is added, keep the heat low and only warm the curry through. Boiling the sauce vigorously after adding cream can cause it to split or curdle.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of Indian breads and rice. Here are some classic serving suggestions:
*   **Naan Bread:** The soft, pillowy texture of fresh naan is perfect for soaking up every last drop of the rich sauce. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly delightful.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Aromatic steamed basmati rice or a simple jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast to the creamy curry and helps to extend the meal.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** For a lighter option, whole wheat roti or flaky paratha are excellent choices.
*   **Accompaniments:** A side of cooling cucumber raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices), a simple kachumber salad (diced onion, tomato, cucumber), or sliced red onions can provide a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the curry.
*   **Garnish:** Always finish your Butter Chicken with a generous sprinkling of fresh chopped cilantro and, if desired, a swirl of extra cream or a small pat of butter for presentation and added richness.

## Variations and Substitutions for Murgh Makhani

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect as is, there are several ways to adapt it to dietary needs or personal preferences:
*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Easily transform this dish into Paneer Makhani by replacing the chicken with cubes of paneer (Indian cottage cheese), which can be lightly fried before adding to the sauce. Tofu can also be used for a plant-based option.
*   **Vegan Version:** For a fully vegan Butter Chicken, substitute butter with plant-based butter or oil, and use a plant-based cream (like full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream) instead of dairy cream. Omit the chicken and use chickpeas, mixed vegetables, or pan-fried plant-based chicken substitutes.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to control the heat. For a spicier kick, you can add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a chopped green chili to the sauce. For milder, use only Kashmiri chili powder for color without much heat.
*   **Healthier Options:** To reduce the fat content, you can decrease the amount of butter and cream, or use a lighter cream or even a portion of milk. Coconut milk can also be a good substitute for heavy cream, offering a slightly different but still delicious flavor profile.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a nut allergy, you can substitute the cashews with sunflower seeds (soaked) or simply omit them and rely on a very well-cooked and blended onion-tomato base for thickness, perhaps with a tablespoon of cornstarch slurry if needed.

Butter Chicken is more than just a dish; it's an experience. Its enduring popularity is a testament to its perfectly balanced flavors and comforting appeal. With this guide, you now have all the knowledge and tips to create a truly classic Murgh Makhani that will impress your family and friends and transport their taste buds straight to the heart of India. Enjoy the culinary journey!
